# Testing Strategies for AI-Assisted Codebases

This dimension covers how testing should adapt when AI writes code and tests.

## Mutation Testing at Scale: Meta's ACH System

Meta deployed LLM-powered mutation testing for privacy compliance (Oct-Dec 2024) [9]:
- Privacy engineers accepted **73%** of generated tests
- **36%** of generated tests were privacy-relevant
- Equivalence detector: Precision 0.95, Recall 0.96 (with preprocessing)
- Platforms: Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Quest, Ray-Ban Meta glasses
- Language: Kotlin

Key insight: Mutation testing generates domain-specific, realistic mutants without the traditional barriers that prevented mutation testing at scale [9]. The 73% acceptance rate demonstrates practical viability in production environments.

**Caveat:** This is domain-specific (Kotlin privacy testing). Generalizability to security-focused mutation testing across other languages is uncertain.

## Property-Based Testing: PGS Framework

The PGS (Property-Generated Solver) framework demonstrated significant improvements over TDD approaches [10]:

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Relative pass@1 gains over TDD | 23.1–37.3% |
| PBT correction rate | 75.9% |
| Public test correction rate | 46.6% |
| HumanEval best (DeepSeek-R1-32B) | 97.6% pass@1 |
| LiveCodeBench absolute improvement | 9.2% |
| Property generation accuracy | 48.9–82.4% |

PBT is positioned as a mitigation for the **tautological test problem**: properties are specification-level constraints harder to make tautological than example-based unit tests. The 75.9% vs 46.6% correction rate gap suggests independent property constraints catch failures that example tests miss [10].

**Caveat:** Benchmarks (HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench) are algorithmic problems, not production codebases. Preprint, not peer-reviewed at time of fetch.

## The Tautological Test Problem

When AI generates both code and tests, both outputs share the same reasoning flaws. Evidence:
- AI-authored PRs have 1.75x more logic/correctness issues than human PRs [7]
- AI-assisted developers wrote less secure code but felt more confident [3]
- Task inexperience led to 26% higher rate of following erroneous automated advice [14]

No source uses the exact term "tautological test," but the pattern is consistently documented: AI-generated tests validate the AI's interpretation rather than actual requirements.

**Mitigations:**
1. Property-based testing (specification constraints independent of implementation) [10]
2. Mutation testing (validates test quality, not just coverage) [9]
3. Human-written test specifications with AI-generated implementations
4. RCI technique: 2 iterations of self-review can reduce weaknesses "by an order of magnitude" [20]

## Security-Explicit Prompts Are Insufficient for Test Quality

From [2]: Security-explicit prompts reduced vulnerability rate by only 4 percentage points (64.8% to 60.8%). This implies that prompt engineering alone cannot make AI-generated tests reliably security-aware.

## OpenSSF Testing Recommendations

The OpenSSF guide [20] recommends:
- Generate unit tests AND negative tests for security functions
- Include SAST/DAST and dependency checks in CI/CD pipelines
- Tag AI-generated code blocks; document tools used
- "Persona patterns" (telling AI to act as security expert) produce WORSE outcomes
- Assume AI-generated code contains vulnerabilities

## Iterative Refinement Can Degrade Security

Discovery agents reported (from IEEE-ISTAS 2025, not directly fetched): 400 code samples across 40 rounds showed security vulnerabilities frequently persist and increase through iterative LLM feedback loops without human intervention. This suggests that iterative code-test cycles without external validation can compound errors.
